levels.title: Technology in One Level
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what technology is and how a few big inventions changed daily life.

levels.title: What Energy Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain energy as the ability to do work and name its main forms.

levels.title: Electricity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain electric current as moving charges and what voltage means.

levels.title: Circuits
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a simple circuit works and what a switch does.

levels.title: The Light Bulb
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how old filament bulbs and modern LEDs make light.

levels.title: Batteries
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a battery stores energy in chemicals.

levels.title: Magnets and Motors
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how magnets and electricity together make a motor spin.

levels.title: Generators
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how spinning magnets inside coils of wire generate electricity.

levels.title: Edison, Tesla and AC
levels.objective: After this level you can explain alternating current and why it won out over direct current.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Energy and Electricity
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how electricity is made, stored and used to do work.

levels.title: The Power Grid
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how electricity travels from a power plant to your wall socket.

levels.title: Coal and Gas Plants
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how burning fuel boils water to spin turbines.

levels.title: Oil
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how oil forms, how it is drilled and what refining does.

levels.title: Nuclear Power
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how splitting atoms heats water in a nuclear power plant.

levels.title: Hydropower
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how dams turn falling water into electricity.

levels.title: Wind Power
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how wind turbines work and where they work best.

levels.title: Solar Power
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.

levels.title: Storing Energy
levels.objective: After this level you can explain why storing electricity is hard and how big batteries help.

levels.title: Energy and Climate
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the ways we make energy affect carbon emissions.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Power for the World
levels.objective: After this level you can compare the main ways the world makes electricity and their trade-offs.

levels.title: Levers, Wheels and Pulleys
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how simple machines make work easier.

levels.title: The Steam Engine
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a steam engine turns heat into motion.

levels.title: The Industrial Revolution
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how steam power and factories changed the way people worked.

levels.title: The Car Engine
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a four-stroke engine turns fuel into motion.

levels.title: Electric Cars
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how electric cars work and how they differ from gas cars.

levels.title: Friction and Brakes
levels.objective: After this level you can explain friction and how brakes stop a moving car.

levels.title: Gears
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how gears trade speed for force.

levels.title: Hydraulics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how liquid under pressure lets a small push lift a heavy load.

levels.title: Why Bicycles Stay Up
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what keeps a moving bicycle upright.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Engines and Motion
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how machines and engines turn energy into motion.

levels.title: How Planes Fly
levels.objective: After this level you can explain lift, thrust, drag and weight.

levels.title: Jet Engines
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how jet engines push planes forward.

levels.title: Trains and High-Speed Rail
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how modern trains, including high-speed trains, work.

levels.title: Why Ships Float
levels.objective: After this level you can explain buoyancy and how a steel ship floats.

levels.title: Radar and Sonar
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how radar and sonar find things by bouncing waves off them.

levels.title: Rockets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how rockets push themselves forward in the vacuum of space.

levels.title: GPS
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how GPS satellites and precise clocks find your position.

levels.title: Traffic
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how traffic lights and road design keep cars moving safely.

levels.title: Self-Driving Cars
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how self-driving cars sense the road around them.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Getting Around
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how planes, trains, ships and satellites move people and find the way.

levels.title: The Printing Press
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Gutenberg's press made books cheap and spread ideas.

levels.title: The Telegraph
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how the telegraph sent messages as electric pulses.

levels.title: The Telephone
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how early telephones turned voices into electric signals.

levels.title: Radio
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how radio sends sound through the air as waves.

levels.title: Television
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how television pictures were first sent and shown.

levels.title: Cameras
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a camera captures light, on film and on a sensor.

levels.title: How a Screen Works
levels.objective: After this level you can explain pixels and how a screen mixes red, green and blue light.

levels.title: Cell Phones
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how cell towers pass a call from one area to the next.

levels.title: What's Inside a Smartphone
levels.objective: After this level you can name the main parts inside a smartphone and what each one does.

levels.title: Milestone: Energy to Information
levels.objective: After this level you can connect electricity, engines and communication into one story of modern technology.

levels.title: What a Computer Is
levels.objective: After this level you can explain input, processing, memory and output.

levels.title: Binary
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how ones and zeros can stand for numbers, letters and pictures.

levels.title: The Microchip
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how transistors on a chip act as tiny switches.

levels.title: Memory and Storage
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the difference between working memory and long-term storage.

levels.title: Software and Code
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what code is and how programs tell a computer what to do.

levels.title: Algorithms
levels.objective: After this level you can explain algorithms as step-by-step instructions, using sorting as the example.

levels.title: The First Computers
levels.objective: After this level you can describe Babbage's engines, Ada Lovelace and the first electronic computers.

levels.title: From Rooms to Pockets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how computers shrank from whole rooms to desks to pockets.

levels.title: Operating Systems
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what an operating system does.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Computers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a computer turns switches, code and memory into useful work.

levels.title: How the Internet Began
levels.objective: After this level you can describe ARPANET and how the internet grew from it.

levels.title: Packets
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how data travels in small packets that each find their own way.

levels.title: Undersea Cables
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how most internet traffic crosses the oceans through cables.

levels.title: Wi-Fi
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Wi-Fi uses radio waves to connect devices at home.

levels.title: The Web
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the difference between the internet and the World Wide Web.

levels.title: Search Engines
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how search engines find pages and rank them.

levels.title: The Cloud
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what the cloud really is: computers in data centers.

levels.title: Encryption
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how encryption keeps messages private.

levels.title: Passwords and Hacking
levels.objective: After this level you can explain common attacks on accounts and how to protect yours.

levels.title: Checkpoint: The Internet
levels.objective: After this level you can trace a message from your device across the internet and explain how it stays private.

levels.title: Refrigerators
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a fridge moves heat out instead of making cold.

levels.title: Microwave Ovens
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how a microwave oven heats food.

levels.title: Clean Water
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how water is cleaned before it reaches your tap.

levels.title: Sewers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how sewers and treatment plants deal with waste water.

levels.title: Heating and Cooling
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how heat pumps and air conditioners move heat.

levels.title: Vaccines
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how vaccines train the immune system.

levels.title: Seeing Inside the Body
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how X-rays, CT scans and MRI see inside the body.

levels.title: Antibiotics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how antibiotics kill bacteria and why resistance matters.

levels.title: Plastics
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what plastic is made from and why it lasts so long.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Home and Health
levels.objective: After this level you can explain the technology behind clean water, kitchens and modern medicine.

levels.title: Skyscrapers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how steel frames let buildings rise so high.

levels.title: Elevators
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how elevators and their safety brakes made tall buildings practical.

levels.title: Bridges
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how beam, arch and suspension bridges carry their loads.

levels.title: Concrete
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what concrete is and why both the Romans and modern builders rely on it.

levels.title: Tunnels
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how tunnels are dug under cities and seas.

levels.title: Steel
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how iron becomes steel and why steel changed building.

levels.title: The Assembly Line
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how Ford's assembly line made cars cheap.

levels.title: Factory Robots
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what factory robots do and how they are programmed.

levels.title: 3D Printing
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how 3D printers build objects layer by layer.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Building and Making
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how modern materials and machines build cities and products.

levels.title: Artificial Intelligence
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what AI is and how machine learning learns from examples.

levels.title: How Chatbots Work
levels.objective: After this level you can explain in simple terms how language models predict text.

levels.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how VR and AR headsets create or add to what you see.

levels.title: Drones
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how drones fly and what they are used for.

levels.title: Gene Editing
levels.objective: After this level you can explain in simple terms what CRISPR gene editing does.

levels.title: Fusion Power
levels.objective: After this level you can explain how fusion differs from fission and why it is so hard to achieve.

levels.title: Quantum Computers
levels.objective: After this level you can explain what makes quantum computers different, without the hype.

levels.title: Space Tech on Earth
levels.objective: After this level you can name everyday technologies that came out of space research.

levels.title: Judging New Technology
levels.objective: After this level you can weigh the benefits and risks of a new invention.

levels.title: Mastery Challenge: Everyday Technology
levels.objective: After this level you can demonstrate command of Everyday Technology Levels 1–99 across the whole tree.
